source_pages: Chapter 3 (Stage 1): guide pages 21-48 (text file PAGE 23-50). Chapter 11 Appendix 3 case studies: guide pages 143-157 (text file PAGE 145-159).

process_characterization_report_structur.content: State that Stage 1 (Process Design) determines the commercial manufacturing process; link enhanced product/process understanding to patient needs and to enabling successful validation. Reference FDA 2011 PV Guidance expectation of 'sufficient understanding to provide a high degree of assurance' (PAGE 23).

Prospective summary of drug-product quality characteristics (safety/efficacy, administration form, dosage, purity, container-closure) per ICH Q8(R2); QTPP is the Voice-of-the-Customer starting point for design space and control strategy (PAGE 33, 40-41).

process_characterization_report_structur.section: 3. Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) identification & criticality rating
process_characterization_report_structur.content: Identify CQAs from the QTPP and rate by criticality (patient safety, release kinetics, packaging interaction). Product risk assessment ranks impact of each quality attribute (PAGE 40-41).

process_characterization_report_structur.section: 4. Statistical methods / tools applied in Stage 1
process_characterization_report_structur.content: Document the statistical toolset used: visualization, descriptive statistics, statistical intervals (confidence/prediction/tolerance/Bayesian), sampling plans, Monte Carlo simulation, MSA (R&R), hypothesis testing, empirical & first-principle models, and DoE (PAGE 24-26).

Identify and, where possible, induce sources of input variability (batch size, site, DS/excipient batches at range ends, equipment sets, operators, hold/processing times, etc.); categorize each input's understanding as low/medium/high risk (high must be mitigated before Stage 2.2). Capture in a version-controlled variability summary tool (Table 3.1) or color-map matrix (Fig 3.2) (PAGE 26-29).

Summarize development, clinical, tech-transfer, engineering, and stability batches (or prior-knowledge commercial batches); describe how they inform process capability/reproducibility and the number/justification of Stage 2.2 batches via visual/summary comparisons, combined statistical intervals, or Bayesian priors (PAGE 28-30).

Iterative science- and risk-based QRA mapping unit operations x parameters x CQAs (e.g., Low/Medium/High ranking grid, Fig 3.7); identifies confirmed risks needing control and knowledge gaps needing DoE. Risk assessment updated after experiments (PAGE 34-35).

process_characterization_report_structur.section: 8. Design of Experiments and Design Space determination
process_characterization_report_structur.content: Describe DoE work flow to establish CPPs, CMAs, intermediate CQAs, interactions, and the multivariate design space; distinguish PAR and NOR (NOR a subset of PAR/design space) and knowledge space vs design space (Fig 3.4). Verify/validate design-space models (PAGE 31-36).

Classify input parameters (e.g., critical / key / non-key controlled parameters) and outputs (IPCs, IPTs, IPMs); document ranges tested in development and control ranges for GMP manufacturing in Process Parameter Reports approved prior to PPQ (Case Study 2, PAGE 150, 152).

Planned set of controls linking CQAs-unit operations-CPPs/CMAs-intermediate CQAs to actual controls (Table 3.5), including analytical, engineering, automation, PAT, and procedural controls; expand to Manufacturing Control Strategy (equipment, facility, GMP, utilities, cleaning) and identify Critical Aspects (PAGE 37-43).
Formally communicate PV steps/deliverables; structure includes scope, references, responsibilities, risk management, and methodology (EU Annex 15 Cl. 1.4/1.5) (PAGE 44).

Risk assessment and PV Stage 1 checklist confirming CQAs & limits determined, CPP ranges stressed, CQA-unit-operation-CPP map, critical raw materials/variability, design space & multivariate interactions identified and models verified, scale effects explored, extended control strategy (hold times), control strategy risk assessment finalized, knowledge-management plan, and VMP in place (Table 3.8, PAGE 47).

risk_assessment_guidance: Risk assessment is the backbone that feeds characterization and the control strategy. Design space is established via an iterative science- and risk-based approach: Step 1 is a Quality Risk Assessment identifying potential CMAs and CPPs (e.g., Low/Medium/High impact grid, Fig 3.7); DoE then confirms CPPs/CMAs/intermediate CQAs and interactions, and the risk assessment is UPDATED after experiments/analysis to reflect the DoE outcome (PAGE 34-36). In Stage 1 the level of understanding of each input is categorized as low or medium risk; HIGH-risk items must be mitigated before Stage 2.2, low-risk items are verified at Stage 2.2 execution, and medium-risk items may lead to continued assessment in Stage 2.2 and additional testing/monitoring in Stage 3 (PAGE 24). The process risk assessment (e.g., process FMECA/FMEA using severity, occurrence, detection) provides input to the control strategy, identified risk-control measures, and monitoring setup, and identifies Critical Aspects for the equipment qualification plan (PAGE 41). A pre-Stage 1 baseline risk assessment (leveraging prior formulations, literature, first principles) is compared against a post-Stage 1 assessment; a control strategy risk assessment must be finalized before Stage 2.2 (PAGE 29, 47). Case Study 2 (MabX): numerical 'Impact Factor' and 'Uncertainty Factor' scores yield an RPN that classifies each attribute as CQA or non-CQA; two sequential process risk assessments were run (initial one selects high/medium-risk parameters for characterization studies; second incorporates study + PPQ + structure-activity knowledge). For parameters still high/medium risk after the second assessment, the control strategy was adjusted (control-range changes or added IPCs/tests) to mitigate risk (PAGE 150).
doe_and_statistics_guidance: Statistics is described as 'the science of making decisions in the face of uncertainty.' Stage 1 statistical methodologies (PAGE 24-26): Visualization (y vs x, x1 vs x2; trending y/x vs time; histogram, stem-and-leaf, box plot, Pareto); Simple Descriptive Statistics (central tendency + dispersion; attribute proportions/percentages); Statistical Intervals - Confidence (e.g., 95% CI on the mean), Prediction, Tolerance (e.g., a 95/90 tolerance interval bounds 95% of the population with 90% confidence), Bayesian Credible and Bayesian Prediction intervals; Sampling Plans (sample size, location, method); Monte Carlo Simulation; Measurement System Analysis / R&R (bias, linearity, stability, precision, accuracy, repeatability, reproducibility); Hypothesis Testing (p-value, typical threshold p <= 0.05, with cautions that p > threshold does not prove the null and statistical significance != practical significance); Empirical/data-driven models (simple linear regression, regression trees, partial least squares regression, support vector machine); and First-principle/fundamental models. DoE (PAGE 26): a highly-used QbD tool giving a systematic approach to study prioritized factors/parameters and establish relationships with quality/in-process attributes; its strength is estimating factor interactions (which OFAT cannot) and maximizing information for the minimum number of runs. Stage 1 studies span laboratory-, pilot-, and large-scale batches. Case Study 2 concrete DoE designs (PAGE 151): Production bioreactor Screening DoE = five-factor, two-level, resolution V fractional factorial, 20 runs at laboratory scale; Response Surface Model DoE = face-centered, four-factor central composite design, 11 runs at laboratory scale; a 3 L scale-down model (same functions/design as the 15,000 L production bioreactor) was used. Case Study 1 statistics: control charts / individual-measurement charts (Western Electric SPC rules noted as not yet applicable with few batches), Cpk; parameters at/near LOD/LOQ, non-normal, or pass/fail are excluded from SPC and instead trended/handled by the quality system; a computed lower control limit of 84.396 confirmed the >= 85% purity acceptance criterion was appropriately set (PAGE 145-148).

key_terms.definition: A prospective summary of the quality characteristics of a drug product that ideally will be achieved to ensure the desired quality, taking into account safety and efficacy (ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 33).

A physical, chemical, biological or microbiological property or characteristic that should be within an appropriate limit, range, or distribution to ensure the desired product quality (ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 33).
A process parameter whose variability has an impact on a CQA and therefore should be monitored or controlled to ensure the process produces the desired quality (ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 33).

A critical quality attribute of a material (raw, feed, solvent, in-process, intermediate, excipient, drug substance, packaging, etc.) whose variability has an impact on a CQA and therefore should be monitored or controlled (PAGE 33).

The multidimensional combination and interaction of input variables (e.g., material attributes) and process parameters demonstrated to provide assurance of quality; working within it is not a change, movement out is a change (ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 33).

A planned set of controls, derived from current product and process understanding, that ensures process performance and product quality (parameters/attributes, IPCs, specifications, monitoring methods/frequency) (ICH Q10 / ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 33).

A characterised range of a process parameter for which operation within this range, while keeping other parameters constant, results in producing material meeting relevant quality criteria (ICH Q8(R2)) (PAGE 34).

Region around the target operating conditions that contains common operational variability (that can't always be controlled) (EMA); a subset of PAR or of ranges derived from a multivariate design space (PAGE 34).

Functions, features, abilities, and performance/characteristics of manufacturing systems necessary to ensure consistent product quality and patient safety; identified/documented from scientific product and process understanding (ASTM E2500) (PAGE 41).

A quality attribute of an intermediate stage that has a direct impact on a final product CQA (e.g., blend uniformity impacts final content uniformity); may be measured by a process analyzer or indirectly by a process indicator (PAGE 41).

Company document capturing process parameters with ranges tested in development and control ranges for GMP manufacturing (upstream and downstream); approved prior to the PPQ campaign and updated after PPQ with revised classifications/ranges (Case Study 2, PAGE 150).

An input process parameter that impacts product quality within a unit operation and may also affect process performance; has operating ranges and action limits; exceeding the action limit triggers a deviation (company-specific term, PAGE 152).
An input process parameter that may affect process performance (e.g., yield) but is unlikely to affect product quality; has operating ranges and action limits (deviation on exceedance) (PAGE 152).
An input process parameter unlikely to impact either process performance or product quality; has operating ranges only (PAGE 152).

Output classifications: In-Process Controls (steps/adjustments during production to keep the process in control), In-Process Tests, and In-Process Measurements; IPCs and IPTs further classified as critical (CIPC/CIPT) or not (PAGE 152).

The expanded overarching control strategy used during commercial manufacturing that connects CQA/CMA/CPP controls with equipment, facility, utilities, cleaning, process control systems, and other GMP controls (subject to inspection) (PAGE 42-43).

case_study_parameters: CASE STUDY 1 (AEX anion-exchange column chromatography, product 'AEX'/'AEX') - In-Process Controls (NOR): Packed Bed Height 32.0 +/- 2.0 cm; Number of cycles since last passing HETP test < 5; Total Number of Previous Uses on Resin < 32; Column Backpressure during Equilibration/Load/Wash/Elution <= 25 psig; Outlet pH (offline) at End of Equilibration 5.0 +/- 0.2; Protein Load per Volume of Resin <= 20 g/L (PAGE 144)

CASE STUDY 1 - In-Process Acceptance Criteria: Eluate Endotoxin Alert Limit >= 5 EU/mL, Action Limit >= 10 EU/mL; Eluate Bioburden Alert Limit >= 10 CFU/10 mL, Action Limit >= 50 CFU/10 mL; Step Yield (A280) >= 75%; Eluate Purity (RP-HPLC) >= 85% (PAGE 144)
CASE STUDY 1 - Additional sampling: Eluate Host Cell Protein Content < 500 ng/mL; Eluate DNA Content < LOQ (PAGE 144)

CASE STUDY 1 - Four parameters carried into formal CPV: eluate endotoxin, eluate bioburden, step yield, eluate purity (RP-HPLC); data from 10 batches (2 representative engineering + 3 PPQ + lots 001-008) (PAGE 145)

CASE STUDY 1 - Step yield data: engineering 90, 89%; PPQ 91, 92, 90%; lot 004=91%, lot 005=76% (out-of-control, below LCL though >= 75% IPAC met; cause: operator switched to waste fraction prematurely, Target 0.2 AU vs Actual 0.5 AU); lots 006-008 = 92, 90, 92% (PAGE 146-147)
CASE STUDY 1 - RP-HPLC eluate purity data (10 lots): 90, 89, 92, 90, 93, 90, 91, 88, 90, 93%; computed lower control limit = 84.396% confirms the >= 85% acceptance criterion (PAGE 148)

CASE STUDY 2 (MabX cell culture mAb) - Production bioreactor process characterization used a 3 L scale-down model; Screening DoE = five-factor two-level resolution V fractional factorial, 20 runs (lab scale); RSM DoE = face-centered four-factor central composite design, 11 runs (lab scale) (PAGE 151)

CASE STUDY 2 - Input parameters studied (production bioreactor screening): Bioreactor Temperature, Bioreactor pH, Bioreactor Dissolved Oxygen, Day 0 Seed Density, Medium Concentration (all High Risk); Medium Concentration dropped after screening (PAGE 150-151)

CASE STUDY 2 - Output parameters and impacting inputs: Peak viable cell density (pH, seed density, temperature, DO); Cumulative integral of cell growth (pH, seed density, temperature, DO); Culture viability (pH, DO); Titer (pH, seed density, temperature, DO); Glycoforms (temperature, pH, DO); Product purity (temperature, pH); Charge/acidic isoforms (temperature, pH, culture duration); Oxidized species (culture duration) (PAGE 151)

CASE STUDY 2 - Three parameters (temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen) impacted product glycoforms (esp. Man5, G0F, G1F), purity, and charge isoforms; higher pH increased %Man5, %sialylation, %peak3 and lower pH raised acidic species; higher temperature raised %acidic species, lower temperature raised %Man5 and %peak3; increased DO increased %Man5 and impacted terminal galactosylation (PAGE 151, 153)

CASE STUDY 2 - Controlled parameters (production bioreactor): Bioreactor Temperature Storage/Equilibration (°C) = Key; Bioreactor pH Post Equilibration Storage = Key; Transfer Time to Inoculate (hours) = Key pre-PPQ, downgraded to Non-Key post-PPQ; Seed Density (viable cells/mL) = Critical pre-PPQ, reclassified to Key post-PPQ; Online pH Day 0-Harvest = Critical; Online Temperature (°C) = Critical; Online Dissolved Oxygen (%) Days 0-5 = Key, Days 5-Harvest = Critical; Agitation Days 0-10 (rpm) = Key; Nutrient Feed Media Daily Amount (L) = Key; Maximum Total Antifoam Added (kg) = Key; Culture Duration (days) = Critical at upper end / Key at lower end (PAGE 152-153)

CASE STUDY 2 - IPCs: Culture Viability Stage L Day 0 (%), Culture Viability Stage L Day 10 (%). IPTs: Stage L Harvest Titer (mg/L). CIPTs: Harvest CNC (Confirmation of No Contamination), In Vitro Adventitious Virus, Mycoplasma; Day 5 and Harvest MMV Q-PCR (CIPT pre-PPQ, IPT post-PPQ) (PAGE 154)

CASE STUDY 2 - Manufacturing scale: three equivalent bioreactor trains, each with four seed-train bioreactors (60 L, 235 L, 950 L, 3,750 L) and two 15,000 L production bioreactors; two purification suites; PPQ campaign = five batches (MabX-001 to 005) on Trains T2/T3, Harvest Area 2, Purification Suite P1 (PAGE 155-156)
